title: Python Compatibility and Canonical Rust-Core Cutover

preflight.note: Created before Python/Rust authority cutover; activated after WI053-WI055 completed and Decision 0042 selected the versioned Rust stdio engine boundary. Temporarily blocked on 2026-09-10 by WI057 after an operator reproduced a host-impacting Git process/refresh amplification defect. Reactivated after WI057 corrected the snapshot/session/process substrate and native operator validation completed successfully.

acceptance_criteria.text: Record and implement Decision 0042's surface-scoped authority map: Rust becomes canonical for the WI053/WI054-proven repository/validation/dashboard/graph/analysis/typed-work-mutation semantics, while explicitly unmigrated Python and WI050 surfaces remain separately identified.

Evaluate PyO3/native-extension and stable executable/protocol compatibility against current Python/Rust packaging realities and document why the selected versioned local stdio JSON executable protocol is the primary Python/language-neutral compatibility seam rather than an accidental implementation preference.

Add a reusable Rust protocol/version DTO boundary and a dedicated `repopact-engine` machine executable that accepts one deterministic JSON request on stdin, returns one structured JSON response on stdout, keeps non-protocol logs on stderr, and introduces no daemon/network/repository-local persistent state.

The engine protocol provides handshake/capabilities, protocol-major and product-version identity, request-id echo, structured diagnostics/errors, explicit unsupported-operation behavior, and semantic-result distinction from transport/protocol failure; Python never parses human Rust CLI text as semantic protocol.

Engine mutation operations accept only high-level typed semantic intent and invoke the WI054 Rust plan/apply boundary internally; the protocol exposes no arbitrary filesystem write/JSON Patch authority and does not execute a caller-round-tripped raw `MutationPlan` or caller-supplied file operation set.

Add one Python compatibility client responsible for same-environment engine discovery, explicit development override, handshake, exact packaged product-version verification, protocol-version verification, request IDs, JSON transport, timeout/cancellation, Windows executable handling, and structured error mapping without silent arbitrary-PATH trust.

Migrate public `repopact validate` to canonical Rust engine authority with compatible human diagnostics/exit semantics; missing, malformed, incompatible, or wrong-version engines fail explicitly and never trigger automatic legacy-Python validation fallback.

Flip validation conformance authority so the published fixture expectations are exercised against canonical Rust by default while the historical Python validator remains an explicit independent regression comparator rather than co-canonical authority; preserve the legacy 20-case corpus and separately owned WI050 corpus.

Migrate public `repopact dashboard`, `repopact new work-item`, `repopact work propose`, and `repopact work amend-proposal` to the Rust engine while preserving practical CLI behavior; proposed-only amendment is enforced by Rust semantics, and decision/policy creation remains Python-owned unless separately proven.

For retained Python mutation workflows that perform a final conformance decision, route that final validation through canonical Rust where safe without rewriting the workflows themselves; legacy Python validation/generation code may remain only as explicit regression/reference or unmigrated implementation, not hidden fallback for migrated public commands.

Migrate Python distribution packaging to a Maturin mixed Rust/Python `bin` model or equivalently proven implementation that keeps the `repopact` Python package and console entrypoint while installing a same-release platform-native `repopact-engine` without introducing a PyO3/CPython extension ABI dependency.

Update release-build structural verification from the obsolete `py3-none-any` assumption to strict platform-wheel checks including Python package/import-root integrity, engine executable presence, correct platform/ABI tagging, package/engine version coupling, schemas/templates, absence of flat modules/desktop payload, source-distribution Rust completeness, SHA-256 evidence, clean-tree requirements, and repeat-build reproducibility.

Prove a fresh built wheel in an isolated environment with no checkout on `PYTHONPATH`: wheel installation requires no Rust compiler, the Python CLI resolves its same-environment packaged engine, handshake/version identity passes, and migrated validation/dashboard/work-item commands operate successfully on scratch repositories.

Prove explicit fail-closed compatibility behavior for missing engine, malformed response, unsupported protocol major, product-version mismatch, and unsupported engine operation, with executable evidence that migrated commands do not silently fall back to legacy Python semantics.

Prove and document the source-distribution/source-build path, including Rust/Maturin toolchain requirements and offline/network expectations, while distinguishing compiler-free wheel installation from source builds.

Produce actual Windows platform-wheel/install/runtime evidence on the available host and record deterministic Linux/macOS build instructions/status without claiming unexecuted runtime/package validation; production signing/notarization and frozen CI changes remain separate unless independently authorized.

WI050 admission/approval/guard/enforcement/IPC/platform/protected-service/operator-authority semantics remain on their existing Python/protected-provider authority path, remain 8/8 on their corpus, and are rejected/absent from the generic Rust compatibility engine rather than ported through an unproven shim.

Preserve all relevant WI053-WI055 regressions after cutover: Python test suite, Rust workspace tests, canonical 20-case conformance, legacy Python comparator, WI050 8/8 corpus, linked-worktree/reference parity, desktop adapter/frontend binding/type/test/build checks, and frozen-surface integrity.

Document an executable/package rollback that requires no repository-history rewrite or durable record-format downgrade, and update public/developer claims to distinguish canonical Rust surfaces, Python compatibility/retained surfaces, platform limitations, WI050 status, and unpublished/local artifact status without claiming an all-Rust rewrite.

Closeout evidence records the final main SHA/commits, exact authority map, protocol/version/operations, Python engine discovery and migrated commands, conformance flip, packaging/wheel tags and hashes, fresh-wheel and source-build proofs, no-fallback tests, Windows and Linux/macOS status, rollback, full regression counts, exact deferred surfaces, and whether WI052 is ready for umbrella closeout.
